The 1969–70 season was a rebuilding year, as the Celtics had their first losing record since the [1949–50 season](/wiki/1949%E2%80%9350_NBA_season "1949–50 NBA season"). However, with the acquisition of [Paul Silas](/wiki/Paul_Silas "Paul Silas") and future Hall of Famers [Dave Cowens](/wiki/Dave_Cowens "Dave Cowens")[[40]](#cite_note-41) and [Jo Jo White](/wiki/Jo_Jo_White "Jo Jo White"),[[41]](#cite_note-42) the Celtics soon became dominant again. After losing in the Eastern Conference finals in 1972, the Celtics regrouped and came out determined in 1973 and posted an excellent 68–14 regular season record. But the season ended in disappointment, as they were upset in seven games by the [New York Knicks](/wiki/New_York_Knicks "New York Knicks") in the conference finals. [John Havlicek](/wiki/John_Havlicek "John Havlicek") injured his right shoulder in game six and was forced to play game seven shooting left-handed.[[42]](#cite_note-43) The Celtics returned to the playoffs the next year, defeating the [Milwaukee Bucks](/wiki/Milwaukee_Bucks "Milwaukee Bucks") in the [1974 NBA Finals](/wiki/1974_NBA_Finals "1974 NBA Finals") for their 12th NBA championship.[[43]](#cite_note-44) Boston took a 3–2 series lead and had a chance to claim the title on their home court. The Bucks won Game Six in Boston when [Kareem Abdul-Jabbar](/wiki/Kareem_Abdul-Jabbar "Kareem Abdul-Jabbar") nestled in a hook shot with 3 seconds left in the game's second overtime, and the series returned to Milwaukee. Cowens was the hero in game 7, scoring 28 points, as the Celtics brought the title back to Boston for the first time in five years.

During this meeting, Hu and Wu agreed that both sides should re-commence official dialogue under the 1992 consensus – that "both sides recognize there is only one China, but agree to differ on its definition."
